    • title

      public ContainerRegion.Builder title(Supplier<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> title)
      The section's title, read every frame, drawn where vanilla draws a container's (1 px in, 11 px above the content). Vanilla's key for a vanilla container (Component.translatable("container.shulkerBox")), so a pack that blanks vanilla's titles blanks it too (see "Titles and names").

    • name

      public ContainerRegion.Builder name(Supplier<net.minecraft.network.chat.Component> name)
      What the section is called while its title comes out blank and other sections show, read every frame, in place of its container's own name. Only needed where that falls short: a section's source names it already (the name the player gave it, else its block's, "Lime Shulker Box"), and a section with no source is called by the block the screen was opened on. With neither, vanilla's own English for the title's key.

    • texture

      public ContainerRegion.Builder texture(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier texture)
      The container texture this section stands for where no block says so, a full texture path (ContainerRegion.CHEST, ContainerRegion.SHULKER_BOX, or a mod's own container texture laid out like vanilla's): under a resource pack that restyles it, the section's slot frames and its part of the list take its look. Vanilla's chest by default. A section with a source takes its block's texture instead (a shulker box's for a shulker box, the chest's for a chest, ender chest or barrel), so the two can't disagree; this is for a section with no block behind it (a mod's own slot group, a source from an item that isn't a block, a block of another kind) and for the screen's own container. In that order: the source's block, then this, then the chest.

    • source

      public ContainerRegion.Builder source(Supplier<@Nullable ContainerRegion.Source> source)
      The container this section shows, read every frame. The section takes its texture from its block (see texture) and its name from it (see name), and with OptiGUI installed the pack's rules are evaluated against it, so a lime box's section has the lime art whatever screen it is on. Without a source, the section is the screen's own container: the block the screen was opened on, else what OptiGUI picked for the open screen. A source that gives null (its container not known this frame) takes its texture and what OptiGUI picked for the open screen.

    • onHiddenLanding

      public ContainerRegion.Builder onHiddenLanding(Runnable action)
      What happens when a quick move (a shift-click) lands an item in this section while it is hidden: the region scrolls to a slot only in a shown section, so this is the mod's chance to show it (pick its tab, say). MenuKit shows nothing itself. Render thread.
